US First Lady Melania Trump has "successfully secured" a ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine in the Russian-occupied city of Oleshky, the White House has said.
 
It said the truce in the "front-line war city on the brink of disaster" without medicine, food and clean water would begin on 29 October.
 
Ukraine and Russia confirmed the deal was agreed to evacuate residents and deliver aid. Moscow said its forces would stop firing at 04:00 (02:00 GMT) on 27 October.
 
The statement did not say how long the ceasefire would be in place for.

author: BBC News
description:
The fall of el-Fasher in Sudan in October 2025 was on the most brutal chapters of the civil war that has raged between the government's Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
 
Now, a BBC investigation has found evidence RSF fighters systematically destroyed the city's healthcare system during their long siege and subsequent takeover.
 
UN human rights chief Volker Türk called the findings "deeply disturbing", saying multiple attacks by the Rapid Support Forces (RSF) on civilian infrastructure, including health facilities, were serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes.
 
The RSF rejected BBC's findings. A paramilitary-aligned health minister in Nairobi dismissed the allegations as Sudanese government propaganda.

Subscribe to our channel here: https://bbc.in/bbcnews

author: BBC News
description:
A Metropolitan Police detective who was raped by a fellow officer has told the BBC that Scotland Yard's handling of her case was "like being raped all over again".

Linda Williams, who has waived her right to anonymity for this exclusive interview, was attacked in 2004 by David Carrick, one of the UK’s most notorious sex offenders who was jailed three years ago for attacking Linda and other women. But she says the Met’s conduct during a subsequent civil case left her feeling suicidal.

In an unprecedented move for a serving officer, she is calling for the Commissioner, Sir Mark Rowley, to resign, and says she does not trust her own force to handle cases like hers.

The Met has paid tribute to her and says it tried to reduce her distress and re-traumatisation.

description:
Ukraine is still recording issues with the Starlink network, sources within the defence ministry say, after Donald Trump said limits on the satellite uplink had been reversed by Elon Musk.

The sources told the BBC that instances of drones experiencing connection loss at speeds of 161km/h (100mph) were being recorded, hampering military operations.

The US president had denied instructing the tech billionaire to restrict connectivity to Starlink's military-grade counterpart, Starshield, before saying on Thursday that Musk had "put it back".

Musk previously said he was not behind the slowdown, which affected Ukraine's ability to use attack drones and co-ordinate defensive operations.
